title: Erdős 249 totient-tail toolkit: dyadic rewriting and exact affine-geometric sums

concepts.label: Dyadic power rewrite
concepts.note: Division by 2^n is represented as multiplication by the nth power of 1/2, putting dyadic tails into geometric-series form.

concepts.label: Linear geometric envelope
concepts.note: The sequence j(1/2)^j is summable and provides the growing part of the affine tail majorants used in the period-killer analysis.

concepts.label: Exact affine-geometric total
concepts.note: For every real C, the summable series with terms (C+j)(1/2)^j has exact total 2C+2.

concepts.label: Analytic toolkit authority boundary
concepts.note: These classical series identities license later convergence and tail estimates but contain no arithmetic information about totients or certified period kills.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED ANALYTIC TOOLKIT: for every real a and natural n, a/2^n = a(1/2)^n. The linear geometric series with terms j(1/2)^j is summable. More generally, for every real C the affine-geometric series with terms (C+j)(1/2)^j is summable and its exact sum is 2C+2.
statement_nodes.engine: Rewrite division by powers of two as powers of 1/2; apply the standard geometric first-moment summability theorem; split the affine series into constant-geometric and linear-geometric parts and evaluate both exact totals.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard geometric-series and differentiated-geometric-series identities, specialized at ratio 1/2.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The packet proves only convergence and an exact elementary series evaluation. It does not estimate a totient tail by itself, assert a property of Euler's totient function, fire a certifiedKill, supply certificates for unbounded periods, exclude a rational denominator, or prove irrationality of the Erdős 249 series.
